topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Paradox
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of the secant line over an interval. Use a visual of a cheetah chasing prey to show that 'average speed' hides the dramatic sprints and pauses during the hunt.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed is 20m/s, but at exactly 2 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down?

sections.title: The Limit Approach: From Secant to Tangent
sections.content: Introduce the visual 'shrinking interval' animation. As the two points on the curve get infinitely close (Δt → 0), the secant line morphs into a tangent line at a single point.
sections.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic curve moving toward each other until they overlap, visually transforming the chord into a tangent line.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Introduce the formal definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain this as the 'instantaneous speed' or the slope of the tangent line at exactly point x.
sections.example: Graph of y = x²; show the slope calculation at x=2 transitioning from a secant slope of 5 to the tangent slope of 4.

sections.title: Application: The Robot's Velocity
sections.content: Demonstrate the utility of the derivative. If a cleaning robot's position is a function of time, the derivative allows us to know its exact velocity at any micro-second, preventing it from bumping into walls.
sections.example: A smart robot's position function p(t) = 3t²; calculating p'(t) = 6t to find the robot's exact velocity at t=3 seconds.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = Slope of tangent line = Instantaneous rate of change. Emphasize that while average change looks at the 'big picture,' the derivative provides the 'precise focus' needed for physics and engineering.
sections.example: A 10-second summary animation showing a car speedometer needle moving in sync with the calculated derivative of its position function.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Paradox
lecture_lines: Average speed is total distance over total time.
[Asset: cheetah_run_path] Cheetah covers 100 meters in 5 seconds.
Average speed is 20 meters per second.
But this hides the cheetah's actual movement.
Did it sprint or pause mid-hunt?

Create a Dot #FF0000 at (0,0) representing a moving object.
Move the Dot along a path with constant speed.
Show a distance-time line graph #00FF00.
Highlight a secant line between two distant points.

storyboard.title: The Limit Approach: From Secant to Tangent
lecture_lines: We shrink the time interval toward zero.
[Asset: secant_to_tangent_morph] Secant line connects two points.
As points approach, the interval closes.
The secant line becomes a tangent line.
This reveals the rate at one instant.
animations: Draw a smooth curve #FFFF00 representing position over time.
Place two points A and B on the curve #00FFFF.
Draw a secant line connecting A and B #FF00FF.
Move point B closer to A along the curve.
Show the secant line approaching the tangent line at A.

storyboard.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: Derivative is the limit of the secant.
[Asset: formal_definition_formula] Definition uses h approaching zero.
It calculates slope at a single point.
For x squared, the slope is 4.
This is the instantaneous speed.
animations: Display formula f'(x) = lim h->0 [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h.
Highlight the term f(x+h) - f(x) in color #FF8C00.
Highlight the term h in color #7FFF00.
Animate the fraction as h shrinks to zero.
Blink the final derivative notation #FFFFFF to emphasize.

storyboard.title: Application: The Robot's Velocity
lecture_lines: Robot position follows a specific function.
[Asset: robot_velocity_graph] Velocity is the derivative of position.
Calculated derivative keeps the robot safe.
animations: Display a robot graphic.
Plot the robot's position data points over time.
Calculate the instantaneous velocity using the derivative.

storyboard.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Derivative equals the tangent line's slope.
[Asset: summary_graph] Average change versus instantaneous focus.
Derivative provides precision for engineering.
animations: Flash a summary of the Secant-to-Tangent logic #FF0000.
Display the derivative formula again with highlight #FFFF00.
Fade out with a final takeaway message #FFFFFF.
